evidence.claim: The authentication page is one bounded card at one route for the three authentication journeys.
The connected page implements sign-in, emailed-OTP sign-up, emailed-OTP password reset, two-factor branching, refusal handling and session adoption.
Session state restores on mount and refuses to adopt an auth payload that still requires two-factor verification or lacks an access token.
The interaction test submits sign-in credentials and verifies that an API refusal is rendered.
The signIn mutation accepts email/password, delegates to the service, conditionally sets the refresh cookie, and returns either an access payload or pending two-factor challenge.
Frontend GraphQL operations define sign-up and forgot-password OTP initiation, resend and verification contracts, including the boolean password-reset result.
The backend AuthPayload distinguishes usable access from a pending two-factor challenge and keeps refresh tokens out of the GraphQL payload.
